# tritonctl sandbox

Agent sandboxes: microVMs that run programs for you

Subcommands: list, show, create, update, delete, keepalive, stop, start, pause, resume, resize, fork, snapshot, exec, exec-attach, claude, git, pr, ssh-config, fs, ports, port-forward, url, network, capability, rdp, template

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl sandbox list

List the sandboxes in the project

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox list [OPTIONS]`

- `--state <STATE>`: Only sandboxes in this state (`running`, `failed`, ...) (one of: pending, placing, starting, running, stopping, stopped, pausing, paused, resuming, forking, snapshotting, resizing, deleting, deleted, failed, unknown)
- `--label <KEY[=VALUE]>`: Only sandboxes that carry this label, as `key` or `key=value`

## tritonctl sandbox show

Show one sandbox

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox show [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl sandbox create

Create a sandbox and wait until it runs; `--no-wait` prints it while it is still starting

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox create [OPTIONS] [-- <ARGV>...]`

- `--name <NAME>`: Name. The server makes one when omitted
- `--template <TEMPLATE>`: Template, as `name`, `name:tag` or `name:<build id>`. `base` when omitted
- `--isolation <ISOLATION>`: Isolation tier. The template's own when omitted (one of: unknown, microvm)
- `--package <PACKAGE>`: The sandbox package that sizes it (`sandbox-2g`, `sandbox-4g`, `sandbox-8g`, or one your operator made). The deployment's default when omitted
- `--subnet <SUBNET>`: The subnet the sandbox joins (name or uuid). The project's own when it has exactly one
- `--env <KEY=VALUE>`: An environment variable for the first process, as key=value. Repeatable. Values are never shown again
- `--label <KEY=VALUE>`: A label, as key=value. Repeatable
- `--metadata <KEY=VALUE>`: A metadata entry, as key=value. Repeatable
- `--ttl <DURATION>`: Time from creation to the deadline: `90s`, `30m`, `2h`, `1d`. Every sandbox has a deadline, so zero is refused
- `--idle-timeout <DURATION>`: Time without activity before `--on-deadline` is applied: the sandbox is deleted, or stopped with its filesystem kept. `0` turns this off
- `--on-deadline <ON_DEADLINE>`: What happens at the deadline: `delete`, `stop` or `pause` (one of: delete, stop, pause, unknown)
- `--allow-out <CIDR>`: A destination the sandbox may reach, as a CIDR block or an address. Repeatable. Allow beats deny
- `--deny-out <CIDR>`: A destination the sandbox may not reach. Repeatable
- `--allow-in <CIDR>`: A source that may reach the sandbox. Repeatable
- `--allow-out-domain <NAME>`: A name the sandbox may reach over HTTP and HTTPS. `*.example.com` covers every name below it, not `example.com`. Repeatable
- `--deny-out-domain <NAME>`: A name the sandbox may not reach, in the same form. Deny beats allow. Repeatable
- `--network <FILE>`: The whole policy as a JSON file, or `-` for stdin: `{"allow_out": [...], "deny_out": [...], "allow_in": [...]}`
- `--net <PRESET>`: Add a named set of allowed names to the network policy. `github` allows github.com and the hosts that serve its files (one of: github)
- `--repo <REPO>`: A GitHub repository to clone into /work/NAME once the sandbox runs: `owner/name` or `https://github.com/owner/name`. Adds the `github` network preset
- `--branch <BRANCH>`: The branch to clone. The repository's default when omitted
- `--github-token-env <VAR>`: The local environment variable that holds the GitHub token. Without it the token comes from `gh auth token`
- `--cwd <CWD>`: Working directory of the first process
- `--user <USER>`: Guest user of the first process
- `--no-wait`: Print the sandbox as soon as the server accepts it, while it is still starting, instead of waiting until it runs
- `<ARGV>...`: The first process and its arguments. The template's own when omitted

## tritonctl sandbox update

Change the lifetime, labels or metadata of a sandbox

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox update [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--ttl <DURATION>`: Time from creation to the deadline: `90s`, `30m`, `2h`, `1d`. Every sandbox has a deadline, so zero is refused
- `--idle-timeout <DURATION>`: Time without activity before `--on-deadline` is applied: the sandbox is deleted, or stopped with its filesystem kept. `0` turns this off
- `--on-deadline <ON_DEADLINE>`: What happens at the deadline: `delete`, `stop` or `pause` (one of: delete, stop, pause, unknown)
- `--label <KEY=VALUE>`: Replace every label, as key=value. Repeatable; give `--clear-labels` to remove them all
- `--clear-labels`: Remove every label
- `--metadata <KEY=VALUE>`: Replace every metadata entry, as key=value. Repeatable

## tritonctl sandbox delete

Delete a sandbox

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox delete [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails

## tritonctl sandbox keepalive

Move the deadline of a sandbox later

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox keepalive [OPTIONS] --ttl <DURATION> <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--ttl <DURATION>`: Move the deadline to this long from now. It never moves earlier (required)

## tritonctl sandbox stop

Stop a sandbox and keep its filesystem

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox stop [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--force`: Halt the guest instead of asking it to shut down

## tritonctl sandbox start

Start a stopped sandbox with the filesystem it had, and wait until it runs

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox start [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--no-wait`: Print the sandbox as soon as the server accepts the start, instead of waiting until it runs

## tritonctl sandbox pause

Save a running sandbox's memory and disk and stop its VM; a resume continues every process where it was

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox pause [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl sandbox resume

Continue a paused sandbox where it was, and wait until it runs

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox resume [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--ttl <TTL>`: Seconds from now to the new deadline. It only moves later

## tritonctl sandbox resize

Move a stopped sandbox to another sandbox package

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox resize [OPTIONS] --package <PACKAGE> <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--package <PACKAGE>`: The sandbox package to move to. The sandbox must be stopped; the disk never shrinks (required)

## tritonctl sandbox fork

Make new sandboxes whose filesystem is a copy of this one's, on the same host. Each child gets its own address

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox fork [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--count <COUNT>`: How many children to make (default: 1)
- `--name-prefix <NAME_PREFIX>`: Children are named with this prefix
- `--ttl <DURATION>`: Time from creation to each child's deadline
- `--kind <KIND>`: What each child keeps: `filesystem` or `memory` (one of: filesystem, memory, unknown; default: filesystem)
- `--from-snapshot <SNAPSHOT>`: Clone from this snapshot of the sandbox (name or uuid) instead of one taken now
- `--label <KEY=VALUE>`: A label for each child, as key=value. Repeatable
- `--no-wait`: Print the children as soon as the server accepts them, while they are still starting, instead of waiting until each runs

## tritonctl sandbox exec

Run a program in a sandbox and stream its output.

The exit status is the program's own, or 128 plus the signal number. Ctrl-C sends SIGINT to the program, and a second Ctrl-C sends SIGKILL; the sandbox keeps running. A third Ctrl-C leaves without waiting for the program.

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox exec [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> [-- <ARGV>...]`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--cmd <LINE>`: A shell line, run as `/bin/sh -lc LINE`, instead of an argv
- `--cwd <CWD>`: Working directory in the guest
- `--user <USER>`: Guest user to run as
- `--env <KEY=VALUE>`: An environment variable, as key=value. Repeatable
- `--tag <TAG>`: A label to find the exec by later, instead of its id
- `--max-duration <DURATION>`: Kill the program after this long: `90s`, `30m`, `2h`
- `-t, --tty`: Give the program a terminal and attach this one to it, in raw mode. Every key goes to the program, Ctrl-C too; `~.` at the start of a line detaches and leaves the program running. Needs a terminal on stdin
- `-i, --stdin`: Send local stdin to the program, and end its input when local stdin ends. Without this, the program's input is empty
- `-q, --quiet`: Print no summary line and no notices, only the program's output
- `<ARGV>...`: The program and its arguments, after `--`

## tritonctl sandbox exec-attach

Attach again to a program started with `exec`

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox exec-attach [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <EXEC>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<EXEC>`: Exec id, or the tag it was started with
- `--since-stdout <OFFSET>`: Replay stdout from this byte offset (default: 0)
- `--since-stderr <OFFSET>`: Replay stderr from this byte offset (default: 0)
- `--since-pty <OFFSET>`: With `--tty`, replay the terminal stream from this byte offset (default: 0)
- `-t, --tty`: Give the program a terminal and attach this one to it, in raw mode. Every key goes to the program, Ctrl-C too; `~.` at the start of a line detaches and leaves the program running. Needs a terminal on stdin
- `-i, --stdin`: Send local stdin to the program, and end its input when local stdin ends. Without this, the program's input is empty
- `-q, --quiet`: Print no summary line and no notices, only the program's output

## tritonctl sandbox claude

Run Claude Code in a sandbox, on this terminal.

Uses the sandbox named `claude`, made on first use, unless `--sandbox` or `--new` says otherwise. The sandbox may reach the Anthropic API and nothing else. Claude Code comes with the sandbox image; nothing is installed. The credential is read from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and goes only into the environment of the `claude` process, over TLS. Type `~.` at the start of a line to detach; `claude` keeps running.

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox claude [OPTIONS] [-- <CLAUDE_ARGS>...]`

- `--sandbox <SANDBOX>`: The sandbox to use, by name, uuid, or prefix. Without it, the sandbox named `claude`, made on first use
- `--new`: Make a new sandbox, named by `--sandbox` when it is given
- `--subnet <SUBNET>`: The subnet a new sandbox joins, by name or uuid. Needed when the project has more than one. A sandbox that exists already is used only when it is on this subnet
- `--repo <REPO>`: A GitHub repository to clone into /work/NAME once the sandbox runs: `owner/name` or `https://github.com/owner/name`. Adds the `github` network preset
- `--branch <BRANCH>`: The branch to clone. The repository's default when omitted
- `--github-token-env <VAR>`: The local environment variable that holds the GitHub token. Without it the token comes from `gh auth token`
- `<CLAUDE_ARGS>...`: Arguments for `claude`, after `--`

## tritonctl sandbox git

Run git in a sandbox's checkout.

clone, fetch, push and ls-remote get the GitHub token from `gh auth token` or `--github-token-env`, in the environment of this one exec only, and run with hooks off. Others get no token: for a pull, run fetch, then merge.

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox git [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> -- <GIT_ARGS>...`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--repo-dir <DIR>`: The repository directory in the guest. The only clone under /work when omitted
- `--github-token-env <VAR>`: The local environment variable that holds the GitHub token. Without it the token comes from `gh auth token`
- `<GIT_ARGS>...`: git's arguments, after `--`. The subcommand comes first

## tritonctl sandbox pr

Push the checkout's branch and open a GitHub pull request for it. Prints the pull request URL.

The push runs in the sandbox with the token in its environment; the pull request is opened from this host.

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox pr [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--repo-dir <DIR>`: The repository directory in the guest. The only clone under /work when omitted
- `--title <TITLE>`: The title. The subject of the branch's last commit when omitted
- `--body <BODY>`: The description
- `--base <BRANCH>`: The branch to merge into. The repository's default when omitted
- `--draft`: Open the pull request as a draft
- `--github-token-env <VAR>`: The local environment variable that holds the GitHub token. Without it the token comes from `gh auth token`

## tritonctl sandbox ssh-config

Print an ssh_config entry that reaches the sandbox over its tunnel, for ssh, scp and an editor's remote mode.

Makes a key pair for the sandbox on this host, adds the public key to the guest login, starts sshd on the guest's loopback, and pins its host key.

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox ssh-config [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--install`: Write the entry to ~/.ssh/tritonctl/NAME.conf and include that directory from ~/.ssh/config, instead of printing it

## tritonctl sandbox port-forward

Forward a local TCP port to a port in the sandbox.

Each local connection opens its own tunnel. Ctrl-C stops listening.

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox port-forward [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <PORT>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<PORT>`: TCP port in the guest
- `--local <LOCAL>`: Local port to listen on. Defaults to the guest port
- `--bind <BIND>`: Local address to listen on. Anyone who can reach it can reach the guest port (default: 127.0.0.1)
- `--stdio`: Carry one connection on stdin and stdout instead of listening, for an ssh `ProxyCommand`. Nothing else is written to stdout

## tritonctl sandbox url

Print the preview URL of a guest port.

For a private port the URL carries the preview token once; the browser then holds a cookie for that host. Treat it as a secret.

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox url [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX> <PORT>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `<PORT>`: TCP port in the guest
- `--no-token`: Print the bare URL, without the preview token, even for a private port

## tritonctl sandbox capability

What this deployment offers sandboxes, and its limits

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox capability [OPTIONS]`

## tritonctl sandbox rdp

Open a sandbox's desktop over RDP on a local port.

Prints the RDP client line with the login, then carries every connection to the local port to the sandbox. Runs until interrupted.

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox rdp [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--local <LOCAL>`: The local port to listen on (default: 13389)
- `--bind <BIND>`: The local address to listen on. Anyone who can reach it can try the login (default: 127.0.0.1)
